key_insight: This paper introduces SWE-Flux, a repository-level benchmark designed to test whether LLMs can reason about how code actually behaves at runtime, not just how it looks statically. It fills a major gap between snippet-level execution tasks and repo-level code understanding.
problem_solved: Existing benchmarks mostly measure static code comprehension or rely on LLM-based judging, while execution-reasoning datasets are usually limited to short snippets or single functions. This paper addresses the lack of a realistic, repository-level benchmark for dynamic runtime reasoning in real Python projects.
method: Built SWE-Flux as a repository-level benchmark for dynamic execution reasoning.
Collected 480 execution-grounded instances from 12 real Python repositories.
Designed tasks to evaluate whether models can infer runtime behavior from code execution context, not just source text.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this benchmark provides a more realistic way to measure whether coding models can reason about bugs, program flow, and execution outcomes in full repositories. It can help researchers compare models on a harder and more practical capability that matters for debugging, maintenance, and code understanding.

paper_title: Can LLMs Reason About Runtime Behavior? A Repository-Level Dynamic Benchmark
paper_authors: Hamed Taherkhani, Mohammad Abdollahi, Melika Sepidband, Hridya Dhulipala, Tien N. Nguyen
